product_guards: Require source-bound proposals and consistent direct HTML 200 observations for every canonical hop. Resolve only to an observed canonical or self-canonical final master without noindex. Reject loops, ambiguous observations, external hosts and HTTPS downgrades.

Select only one literal root sitemap.xml, including known static directories, with no generator signal. Re-read package configuration and uniquely routed non-shared literal HTML heads before any PUT; current canonicals must match their observed values. Refuse computed heads, scripts, templates, noindex and ambiguous routes without model fallback.

Validate XML with defusedxml before Expat byte-offset parsing and validate output again. Accept urlset only, preserve significant URL path case, query and slash, and reject DTD, sitemap indexes, foreign namespaces and ambiguous loc elements.

Preserve an existing master's entire entry rather than inheriting alias metadata. Remove only the flagged alias entry when the master already exists. If absent, create only a minimal entry without alias lastmod, images or priority; this case is covered by synthetic tests, not the remote cycle.

Preserve all untouched bytes, comments, line endings, extensions and unrelated existing duplicates. Bound source size to 80000 characters and require a readable sitemap blob SHA for the single GitHub PUT.

URL and GitHub free-form previews and confirmation cannot bypass proof checks via cached previews. Individual deep and bulk correction share the deterministic path, without provider requests, AI file selection or billed tokens.

Keep other sitemap families, auditor, catalog and historical correction receipts unchanged. Unverified entries remain explicitly refused rather than being counted as repaired. No automatic main merge or deployment is part of acceptance.

successful_live_cycle.refusals_explanation: The blog slash target is not independently observed as a direct healthy canonical master. canonical-404 points to an absent destination. Neither entry is removed or described as repaired.

independent_countercheck.description: Re-read pinned main, seed and correction branches, both closed draft unmerged PRs and their exact successful builds. Confirm exactly one commit changes only sitemap.xml. Independently parse all retained entries, compare exact output bytes to removal of six known fixture blocks, and compare saved and fresh served XML. Compare prior duplicate HTML bodies and canonicals while normalizing only the actual owned Netlify deployment-id attribute. Re-prepare the baseline and reproduce the exact XML rewrite with writes, models, file selection and quota calls forbidden.
independent_countercheck.initial_checker_failure: XML serialization included inter-entry tail whitespace accumulated by entry removal. Confirmed no node-content difference, then excluded only tails from node comparison while retaining the exact full-byte check. No product source or test assertion changed.

acceptance_inventory.explanation: This family already had an adverse mention in the preceding duplicate-consolidation record. This dedicated measured repair strengthens its evidence without closing another named-reference gap. References are not a count of passed repairs.
acceptance_inventory.after_snapshot: acceptance-after-final.json in the live temporary directory

initial_red.explanation: Includes one duplicate canonical keyword in a new test fixture, subsequently corrected. The failure count is not a count of independent product bugs.

first_implementation_failure.explanation: The new XML-mode dispatch was accidentally inserted in the head-URL helper and did not run in the sitemap helper. Moved the dispatch to its intended function and restored the unrelated helper; no assertion was weakened.

limitations: Owned static-HTML fixture only, not every customer or stack. The conservative route/head preflight refuses scripts, structured data, templates, ambiguous bindings and unsupported generated or multi-file sitemaps. Refusal is not repair coverage.

Native Netlify previews remain noindex, so raw family counts are 0 before and after. The existing exact preview-host/header projection with the saved served sitemap measures indexable scoring, not production indexation.

Two global occurrences remain uncorrected. The remote cycle covers existing masters only; minimal creation and metadata preservation with nontrivial lastmod/extensions are exercised by synthetic tests. Existing unrelated duplicate entries are deliberately left unchanged.

Current literal HTML heads and sitemap SHA are re-read, but this does not prove all later server-side headers or live customer state are unchanged. Network failure remains possible; no cross-file atomicity or auto-merge promise is made.

Other sitemap families retain their existing behavior and still need dedicated acceptance. No production recovery replay, receipt migration, agent deployment, onboarding, scheduler, payment workflow, capacity test or fresh PostgreSQL run is included; the SQLite suite keeps its existing skipped tests.
next_acceptance_check: Validate the next unmeasured sitemap family on an owned rebuilt fixture, including verified destinations and explicit refused controls, then remaining offered families and client onboarding.
